top_story.headline: Customs and Border Protection sole-sources legal staffing from Contact Government Services for litigation over the White House's immigration priorities
top_story.dek: The justification says the order supports lawsuits challenging the agency's implementation of the Secure America Act and its ability to carry out "the White House's priorities."
paragraphs: U.S. Customs and Border Protection plans to place an order with Contact Government Services, LLC without competition for legal staffing and electronic-discovery services. The work is document review and redaction for its Office of Chief Counsel. According to the signed justification, dated September 18, 2026, the services "are related to pending and reasonably anticipated litigation, including litigation challenging CBP's operational implementation of the Secure America Act's directives and ability to execute the White House's priorities." The order falls under a General Services Administration schedule contract, and the agency's legal basis is unusual urgency. The value is redacted. (70B04C26F00001107, justification)

The document describes reviews of "hundreds of thousands if not millions of files," including body-worn-camera video, cellphone data and forensic images, across review platforms such as Relativity and the Justice Department's Civil Online Relativity Application. It says court deadlines are "inflexible and often compressed" and that missing them can bring "monetary sanctions against the Agency and adverse decisions." It also says the agency "has experienced an unanticipated and unexpected rise in discovery and litigation demands that have strained OCC's resources."

Contact Government Services is a Washington, D.C. firm. USAspending shows a federal contract under its name since September 15, 2023. The justification says the order will be funded with fiscal year 2026 one-year operations and support money, and that the requirement will be solicited under Request for Proposal 20150566.

sections.headline: General Services Administration hires the college that leases the building, not a moving company, for a $39,545 equipment move
paragraphs: There were 45 new justifications, 19 of them posted under other notice types. The agency-by-agency list below covers every one that is not in the Top Story or the Extensions section, and 46 repeats from earlier editions were left out. Contact Government Services is in the Top Story; nine incumbent extensions and bridges are in Extensions.
This is a heavy day: five items are worth reading in full.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: General Services Administration gives a $39,545 moving job to the community college that leases the federal building
meta: Junior College District of East Central Missouri (East Central College)
Only one company can do it
blocks.text: The General Services Administration is buying disassembly, moving and eight months of on-site storage for the U.S. Geological Survey in the Rolla, Missouri, federal building. The vendor is Junior College District of East Central Missouri, the building's lessor, not a moving company. It has no federal contract on record under this name in USAspending. The justification says the regional moving agreement with Superior Moving Service lapsed when its schedule contract did, and that construction on the space starts within two weeks. The college subcontracts the moving to Eagan Office Interiors for $19,745 and the storage trailers to Palmer Leasing for up to $19,800.

blocks.title: Navy extends BAE Systems' hold on Virginia-class submarine propulsors with a five-year no-bid contract
meta: Only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Naval Surface Warfare Center Carderock Division
blocks.text: The Naval Sea Systems Command plans a five-year indefinite-delivery contract with BAE Systems for materials, manufacturing, assembly and delivery of Virginia-class submarine propulsors. It follows contract N00167-24-D-0004, and the first order covers material for two propulsors. The justification says an alternate source would face "a minimum of $58M" in equipment, facility, training and qualification costs. It was posted as an Award Notice, which lists $137,658,562 to BAE Systems Land & Armaments L.P., dated September 29.

blocks.title: Marine Corps re-awards a $527,834 training contract without competition after a rival's protest froze the first award
meta: Urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Navy, Marine Corps Installations West
blocks.text: Marine Corps Installations West awarded VTS Aviation LLC a contract on July 24 to simulate foreign adversary helicopters and drones for the Weapons and Tactics Instructor course at Yuma, Arizona. An unsuccessful bidder, VSC, protested to the Government Accountability Office on August 3 (B-424711.1), and the government chose corrective action on August 28. Because re-competing would take 60 to 75 days, the Marine Corps is now awarding the same company a sole-source order for September 23 through October 24. The justification says the stay left a gap "49 days prior to the live-flight phase."

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement renews Hootsuite social media monitoring for three years without competition
meta: Department of Homeland Security, Mission Support Washington
blocks.text: Immigration and Customs Enforcement will buy its Office of Public Affairs a three-year Hootsuite Enterprise subscription through Carahsoft Technology Corp., for September 30, 2026 to September 29, 2029. The justification says only Hootsuite offers its proprietary AI, "Wisdom," "trained on twelve years of historical social media data," and that the agency has about two years of accumulated configuration on the platform. The pipeline has logged two earlier Hootsuite justifications for the agency.

blocks.title: Immigration agency's investigators plan a no-bid telecom surveillance software buy from Pen-Link
meta: Only one company can do it
Department of Homeland Security, Investigations and Operations Support Dallas
blocks.text: Homeland Security Investigations posted a Special Notice of intent to sole-source telecommunications analysis software support from Pen-Link, Limited, citing the software's proprietary nature. The attached requirements list "Title III/wiretaps, pen register/trap and trace (telephonic, email, social media, IP address, WhatsApp), and live ping/GPS locations," at least 500 concurrent users and at least 10 terabytes of data.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Immigration and Customs Enforcement keeps Acentra Health processing detainee medical claims through 2030 without competition
paragraphs: There were nine new extensions or bridges, and four of them were signed within days of a lapse or tied to a protest. Three are written up below and the rest are listed.

blocks.title: Immigration and Customs Enforcement adds up to six more option periods for Acentra Health's detainee medical claims contract without competition
meta: Urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Homeland Security, Detention Compliance and Removals
blocks.text: The Immigration and Customs Enforcement Health Service Corps is adding two 12-month and four 6-month options to the Acentra Health, LLC contract. Acentra pays outside medical providers who treat detainees. The current period ends October 24, 2026 and the first new option starts October 25. The justification says the Department of Veterans Affairs Financial Services Center "abruptly terminated" the support on October 3, 2025, which led to the original direct award. Losing it could cause "severe deterioration, hospitalization, or death," it says. The award notice lists $848,363,106.

blocks.title: Citizenship and Immigration Services extends Cybernamic's classified cybersecurity task order a fourth time while a recompete protest is pending
meta: Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services
blocks.text: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services will keep Cybernamic, LLC on the classified-systems security task order for up to five more months, from October 21, 2026 through March 20, 2027. The task order has already run on 52.217-8 extensions P00023, P00025 and P00026, covering April 21 to October 20. The justification says the successor award, GCACS IV, "has been protested and is currently awaiting decision" at the Government Accountability Office.

blocks.title: National Institutes of Health bridges National Consulting Partners for three months while a protest of its replacement is decided
meta: Urgent need, no time to compete
Department of Health and Human Services, National Institutes of Health
blocks.text: The National Institutes of Health Office of Science Policy is giving National Consulting Partners, LLC a three-month sole-source task order. The justification cites a post-award protest at the Government Accountability Office against the competitively awarded task order. It lists the risk of "disruption in oversight of more than 4,000 Institutional Biosafety Committees."

items: Navy bridges Serco's Joint Staff training contract without competition. The justification blames the time needed to approve a non-fixed-price contract type under Executive Order 14402, and cites about 1,642 full-time-equivalent staff. The award notice lists $24,964,657. (N0018926CD020)

Defense Information Systems Agency extends Tetrad Digital Integrity's key management support for Military Sealift Command without competition. It covers more than 140 global accounts. The value is redacted. (HC102821F0336)

Navy renews Siemens' HyperWorks engineering software support without competition. It was posted as a Special Notice. (N6660427Q0037)

sections.headline: Federal Aviation Administration gives Frequentis USA a $200 million contract for digital remote air traffic towers
paragraphs: There were 375 new award notices; 543 repeats were left out, including ten from the $300 million Defense Healthcare Management Systems Deployment Solutions multi-award, which an earlier edition listed. Most of the rest are Defense Logistics Agency parts awards.

blocks.title: Federal Aviation Administration awards Frequentis USA a single-award $200 million contract for digital remote towers
blocks.text: The Federal Aviation Administration awarded a direct, definitized single-award indefinite-delivery contract to Frequentis USA, Inc. for digital remote towers. The notice cites Section 161 of the 2018 FAA Reauthorization Act and describes remote towers as a way to provide visual flight rules air traffic services at rural and small airports. It was dated September 30.

meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command
blocks.text: Oceaneering International Inc. won a cost-plus contract for maintenance, modernization, product improvements and design support for the Navy's existing Dry Deck Shelter assets. Work is in Chesapeake, Virginia, and Pearl City, Hawaii. It runs through September 2027, or September 2031 if all four options are exercised. It was dated September 28.

sections.headline: Navy tanker charter warns of Red Sea imminent-danger pay as the Army Corps seeks a new Mississippi River lock
paragraphs: There were 212 new solicitations; 187 repeats were left out. This is a heavy day, so four items are written up in full.

blocks.title: Military Sealift Command seeks a Jones Act tanker for a run through the Red Sea, where crews get imminent-danger pay
meta: Department of the Navy, Military Sealift Command
blocks.text: A solicitation file read today on a notice posted earlier says the "Red Sea, the Bab al-Mandeb Straits, and Gulf of Aden are designated imminent danger pay locations" and that crews receive $225 a month while there. The charter was later reopened with December 15-18 laydays.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers seeks bids for a new 1,200-foot lock at Lock and Dam 25 on the Mississippi River
meta: Department of the Army, Army Corps of Engineers St. Louis District
blocks.text: The Army Corps of Engineers solicitation covers a new drilled-shaft 1,200-foot lock in the auxiliary miter gate bay, a 1,200-foot upstream guard wall and a 650-foot downstream guard wall. The existing 600-foot lock stays as an auxiliary chamber. It was listed earlier this month; today's posting is an update.

blocks.title: Border Patrol's training complex at FLETC Artesia gets a new bid deadline of November 6
meta: Department of Homeland Security, Federal Law Enforcement Training Center
blocks.text: Amendment 0002 moves the due date for the U.S. Border Patrol Integrated Training Complex in Artesia, New Mexico, from October 21 to November 6. One task order will be awarded under the DHS NMACC III construction contract. All 21 attached files are access-restricted on SAM.gov, so none have been read.

blocks.title: Marine Raider facilities at Camp Lejeune: Q&A shows bidder disputes over drawings and a radio shielding test
meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Mid-Atlantic
blocks.text: The fixed-price contract for the Marine Raider battalion complex at Stone Bay is funded with $79.5 million on execution and a $71.4 million fiscal 2027 increment, per amendment 0005. A bidder question in the earlier Q&A says certain controlled drawings were "initially released publicly and later removed," which "may have allowed some offerors earlier access." The same Q&A says a shielded space passing every IEEE 299 table on all six sides is "extremely expensive." These are offeror comments in the Q&A file.

items: Army seeks ground ambulance services at Fort Polk. The Q&A says the contractor will use government-provided paper charting forms at no software licensing cost. (W81K00-26-R-A051)

Smithsonian Institution awards CMTA an estimated $6.7 million to build solar arrays for agrivoltaics research. Six proposals were received. (333302-26RF-0010008)

blocks.text: Other flagged notices were Army Corps dredging, dam repair and levee manholes; Navy and Air Force equipment buys; and NASA helium and land-lease notices. sections.headline: Navy Recruiting Command seeks a partner to put Navy materials in high school classrooms in all 50 states
paragraphs: There were 390 new combined notices; 197 repeats were left out. Two items stand out.

blocks.title: Navy Recruiting Command seeks an education partner to distribute Navy lesson plans to 250 teachers
meta: Department of the Navy, Naval Supply Systems Command Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk
blocks.text: This comes from a document read today on a notice posted earlier. The statement of work says the command wants a national education agency to distribute "Navy sponsored educational materials, lesson plans, and product samples directly to classrooms." The partner needs a network for grades 10 to 12 to "connect the Navy brand directly with high school educators, administrators, students, and parents."

blocks.title: Army Intelligence and Security Command seeks 69 security escorts and access-control officers for classified facilities
meta: Department of the Army, Intelligence and Security Command
blocks.text: The five-year indefinite-delivery contract would staff Army Intelligence and Security Command sites: 10 site supervisors, 31 access control officers and 28 security escorts. Amendment 0001 fixed the staffing at 69 full-time equivalents. The work description cites the command's locations in 45 countries and requires Secret clearances. It is an 8(a) set-aside.

items: Navy plans a sole-source buy of USS Makin Island generator long-lead material. Proposals are due October 23. (N5523626R0013)

sections.headline: Defense Department data release: Lockheed Martin's $1.35 billion THAAD missile modification tops the batch of July 20 contracts just made public
paragraphs: From this morning's edition: USAspending.gov is pulled once a day.

There are 39 new awards of $2 million or more, and all 39 are Defense Department awards signed July 20, 2026 and published this week; Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay. There are also 3 large modifications and 2 cuts. Nothing this run was tied to the White House or the Executive Office of the President. The 32 routine actions are listed, each linked, in 'USAspending: Every Other New Award' at the end of the edition.

blocks.text: Chevron USA Inc. had a fuel contract with the Defense Logistics Agency terminated for convenience, removing $13,144,635 in modification P00001. The product is petroleum-based liquid propellants and fuels, and the description is only a number string ('8512233380!'). Signed July 20, 2026 and published this week. (award)

Lockheed Martin Corporation received a $1,354,247,255 modification (P00128), a supplemental agreement for work within scope, on the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense production contract from the Missile Defense Agency. The description is 'TERMINAL HIGH ALTITUDE AREA DEFENSE (THAAD) PRODUCTION CONTRACT.' Signed July 20, 2026 and published this week. (award)

Raytheon Company won a $270,074,234 award from the Department of the Navy, described only as 'FCS MK 99 MOD 14 - USN' and coded as fire control equipment. The record gives nothing more on what is being bought. Signed July 20, 2026 and published this week. (award)

Hyliion Inc received $41,699,946 from the Navy to design, develop, build, test and deliver 2-megawatt and 3-megawatt scale power generation units to the Office of Naval Research, coded as defense research and development. Signed July 20, 2026 and published this week. (award)

Amazon Web Services, Inc. received $3.7 million from the Department of the Air Force for a contract described as securing '100% access to two (2) antennas in Dubbo, Australia,' coded as storage as a service. Signed July 20, 2026 and published this week. (award)

Secmation LLC received $3,181,200 from the Missile Defense Agency under a contract whose entire description is 'WONDERLAND,' coded as defense research and development. Signed July 20, 2026 and published this week. (award)

footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB Apportionments: no new apportionment files were approved between October 15 and 20, and the manifest was unchanged. SAM.gov document coverage: 1,886 attachments on 406 notices; 1,352 were not read, namely 1,258 queued for later editions, 93 access-restricted on SAM.gov and 1 with no extractable text, and 29 reads failed. In total 2,647 files are queued for later editions. About 1,000 links to outside portals (DIBBS, NECO and PIEE, among others) were not followed. Several findings are Haiku summaries not verified against quotes, and the Pen-Link, Hootsuite and GDIT items rest partly on notice text.
